Thanks for the head's up, Naomi / Elena.

Two mitigation options from CS to keep momentum if procurement slips as indicated:

1) Compressed eval: reduce the eval to a 48-hour focused pass that validates latency and correctness on a curated set of 15 prompts. Redwood provides a pre-warmed sandbox and a field engineer for 2 days to speed onboarding.

2) Staggered acceptance: agree an initial "performance acceptance" milestone during the compressed eval and defer broader integration acceptance to a later cutover window (post-PO). This lets Meditech validate the critical SLA first and we can run the integration work under a scoped MSA amendment.

If you decide to pursue option 1 we can provision the sandbox the week of 3/27 and schedule a 2-day run immediately. I'm attaching a draft compressed-timeline doc with the exact milestones.

Attachment: proposed_timeline.v1.docx (docx)

- Procurement earliest PO issuance: 4/08 (per procurement) — moves final GO/NO-GO to week of 4/17
- Security review of SOC2 artifacts: ~10 business days after submission — likely pushes acceptance beyond 4/17
- Customer is open to a compressed eval (48 hours) to validate latency + fidelity; integration acceptance would be deferred

I propose we escalate two asks to unblock to the degree possible:
1) Short-term: approve a field-engineer allocation and sandbox quota for a compressed eval (we can bill as POC credits) — Marissa says she can provision.
2) Exec-level: authorize a one-time close-credit (or price hold) in the event Meditech needs to shift the PO to the next cycle — this reduces the friction of re-pricing at a later date and gives the AE leverage to keep the deal live.

Attached is an inline risk log I maintained while triaging: MAP_v1_20280310.xlsx (see Blockers tab)
